title: Cleverness never found it
hook: the restless, clever mind has never found Him (Anand)

segments.voice: Yesterday, nadar, and your line, given, not grabbed. Today, the opposite of receiving: being clever.

People admire the clever ones. The kid who finds the loophole in the rules. The friend who always knows the shortcut. The person who can argue any side and win. Modern life rewards it: hack your sleep, hack your diet, hack your productivity. There's a life hack for everything. So it's a little startling when a pauri of Anand Sahib looks straight at cleverness and says, flatly, that it has never once found the One. Not rarely. Never. Nobody.
screen: `WE ADMIRE THE CLEVER ONES.` → `THERE'S A HACK FOR EVERYTHING.` → `NEVER ONCE, FOR THIS.`

segments.voice: The pauri opens: ae man chanchal chaturaaee kinai na paaiaa. O restless mind, no one has found him through cleverness. Chanchal means restless, flickering, like a flame in the wind. Chaturaaee is cleverness, cunning. Kinai na paaiaa: no one has found. Then, in paraphrase: listen, my mind. This enticing illusion, maya, has led people astray in doubt, and the One who made that enticing illusion is the One who set it in the world. It's the mind again, addressed directly, as in pauri two. But this time the Guru names the mind's favorite trick. Why would cleverness fail? Because it's a way of getting, and yesterday showed what this tradition says about getting. Cleverness finds angles, works systems, beats the claw machine. But the One isn't a system; you can't outsmart the One who made the game. Guru Nanak says it in the Japji's first pauri too, in paraphrase: you could have a hundred thousand clevernesses, and not one goes with you. The Gurus aren't against intelligence; the Guru Granth Sahib is full of brilliant poetry and sharp thinking. They're against cleverness used as a way around surrender. The restless mind keeps thinking there must be a trick. The way in, Anand keeps saying, is love, and grace, and staying. No trick is needed, and none would work.
screen: `CHANCHAL: RESTLESS, LIKE A FLAME.` · `CHATURAAEE: CLEVERNESS.` · `YOU CAN'T OUTSMART THE GAME'S MAKER.` · `NOT AGAINST THINKING; AGAINST TRICKS.` · then, large: `NOT BY CLEVERNESS.`

segments.voice: Notice one plan that's a bit too clever: a way to get someone to do what you want without asking, a shortcut around something you should just face, a strategy for looking good. Hold it up to the light, then set it down, and picture the plain way instead: asking directly, being seen as you are. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you let it go; if not, notice how much lighter the plain way feels.
Chaturaaee, cleverness. Ae man chanchal chaturaaee kinai na paaiaa: O restless mind, no one has ever found the Lord through chaturaaee.
Your line: not by cleverness. This is one door that doesn't open to a trick. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Sikhs recite this pauri as part of the full forty-pauri Anand Sahib in the morning Nitnem; its opening line is often quoted in Sikh teaching against cleverness and pride in spiritual life.

original.note: Gurmukhi: chaturaaee, cleverness or cunning; Anand says no one has found the Lord through it.

trapdoor: what you thought: a line against smart people.
what it means: the restless mind's favorite trick, cleverness, has never once found the Lord; the way is love and grace.
what a scholar hears: chaturaaee echoes the Japji's 'sahas siaanpaa lakh hohi', thousands of clevernesses; both set human cleverness against hukam and grace.

chat.says: I'm pretty smart. Can't I just think my way to God if I study enough?
options: Anand says no one found the One by cleverness; the way is love, grace and staying.
Yes, the Gurus say sharp study and clever argument are the surest way in.
No, the Gurus were against thinking itself; study only gets in the way.
chat.meaning: Ae man chanchal chaturaaee kinai na paaiaa: no one has found Him by cleverness. The Gurus valued thinking, but not as a trick around surrender.

notes: Pauri number given as 10 and Ang 918 in sources: Keeper to confirm.

Pauri paraphrased ('chaturaaee na paaiaa kinai too sun man meriaa; eh maaiaa mohanee jin et bharam bhulaaiaa; maaiaa ta mohanee tinai keetee jin thagaulee paaeeaa; kurbaan keetaa tisai vittahu jin mohu meethaa laaiaa'). The last line (jin mohu meethaa laaiaa) is left out because its reading varies; the maya line is simplified. Confirm.
'Life hack' framing is a modern illustration.
